ut.2012.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2012.1.1.reviewed_statement: In acute triangle $ABC$, $\angle A < \angle B$ and $\angle A < \angle C$. Let $P$ be a variable point on side $BC$. Points $D$ and $E$ lie on sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, such that $BP = PD$ and $CP = PE$. Prove that as $P$ moves along side $BC$, the circumcircle of triangle $ADE$ passes through a fixed point other than $A$.

ut.2012.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2012.1.2.reviewed_statement: Determine all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for every pair of real numbers $x$ and $y$, $$f(x + y^2) = f(x) + |yf(y)|.$$

ut.2012.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2012.1.3.reviewed_statement: Determine, with proof, whether or not there exist integers $a, b, c > 2010$ satisfying the equation $$a^3 + 2b^3 + 4c^3 = 6abc + 1.$$

ut.2012.1.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2012.1.4.reviewed_statement: There are $2010$ students and $100$ classrooms in the Olympiad High School. At the beginning, each of the students is in one of the classrooms. Each minute, as long as not everyone is in the same classroom, somebody walks from one classroom into a different classroom with at least as many students in it (prior to his move). This process will terminate in $M$ minutes. Determine the maximum value of $M$.

ut.2012.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2012.2.5.reviewed_statement: Consider (3-variable) polynomials $$P_n(x, y, z) = (x - y)^{2n}(y - z)^{2n} + (y - z)^{2n}(z - x)^{2n} + (z - x)^{2n}(x - y)^{2n}$$ and $$Q_n(x, y, z) = \left[(x - y)^{2n} + (y - z)^{2n} + (z - x)^{2n}\right]^{2n}.$$ Determine all positive integers $n$ such that the quotient $Q_n(x, y, z)/P_n(x, y, z)$ is a (3-variable) polynomial with rational coefficients.

ut.2012.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2012.2.6.reviewed_statement: In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $P$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the respective feet of the perpendiculars from $P$ to lines $AB$ and $CD$. Segments $BF$ and $CE$ meet at $Q$. Prove that lines $PQ$ and $EF$ are perpendicular to each other.

ut.2012.2.7.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2012.2.7.reviewed_statement: Determine all positive integers $n$, $n \ge 2$, such that the following statement is true: If $(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)$ is a sequence of positive integers with $a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_n = 2n - 1$, then there is block of (at least two) consecutive terms in the sequence with their (arithmetic) mean being an integer.

ut.2012.2.8.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2012.2.8.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $a, n \ge 1$ such that for all primes $p$ dividing $a^n - 1$, there exists a positive integer $m < n$ such that $p \mid a^m - 1$.

ut.2013.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2013.1.1.reviewed_statement: A social club has $2k + 1$ members, each of whom is fluent in the same $k$ languages. Any pair of members always talk to each other in only one language. Suppose that there were no three members such that they use only one language among them. Let $A$ be the number of three-member subsets such that the three distinct pairs among them use different languages. Find the maximum possible value of $A$.

ut.2013.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2013.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find all triples $(x, y, z)$ of positive integers such that $x \le y \le z$ and $$x^3(y^3 + z^3) = 2012(xyz + 2).$$

ut.2013.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2013.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle with $\angle BCA = 90^\circ$, and let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $C$. Let $X$ be a point in the interior of the segment $CD$. Let $K$ be the point on the segment $AX$ such that $BK = BC$. Similarly, let $L$ be the point on the segment $BX$ such that $AL = AC$. The circumcircle of triangle $DKL$ intersects segment $AB$ at a second point $T$ (other than $D$). Prove that $\angle ACT = \angle BCT$.

ut.2013.1.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2013.1.4.reviewed_statement: Let $f$ be a function from positive integers to positive integers, and let $f^m$ be $f$ applied $m$ times. Suppose that for every positive integer $n$ there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $f^{2k}(n) = n + k$, and let $k_n$ be the smallest such $k$. Prove that the sequence $k_1, k_2, \dots$ is unbounded.

ut.2013.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2013.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Two incongruent triangles $ABC$ and $XYZ$ are called a pair of pals if they satisfy the following conditions:
(a) the two triangles have the same area;
(b) let $M$ and $W$ be the respective midpoints of sides $BC$ and $YZ$. The two sets of lengths $\{AB, AM, AC\}$ and $\{XY, XW, XZ\}$ are identical 3-element sets of pairwise relatively prime integers.
Determine if there are infinitely many pairs of triangles that are pals of each other.

ut.2013.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2013.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Circle $\omega_1$, with diameter $AC$, intersects side $BC$ at $F$ (other than $C$). Circle $\omega_2$, with diameter $BC$, intersects side $AC$ at $E$ (other than $C$). Ray $AF$ intersects $\omega_2$ at $K$ and $M$ with $AK < AM$. Ray $BE$ intersects $\omega_1$ at $L$ and $N$ with $BL < BN$. Prove that lines $AB$, $ML$, $NK$ are concurrent.

ut.2013.2.7.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2013.2.7.reviewed_statement:
In a table with $n$ rows and $2n$ columns where $n$ is a fixed positive integer, we write either zero or one into each cell so that each row has $n$ zeros and $n$ ones. For $1 \le k \le n$ and $1 \le i \le n$, we define $a_{k,i}$ so that the $i^{\text{th}}$ zero in the $k^{\text{th}}$ row is the $a_{k,i}^{\text{th}}$ column. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of such tables with $a_{1,i} \ge a_{2,i} \ge \cdots \ge a_{n,i}$ for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le n$. We associate another $n \times 2n$ table $f(C)$ from $C \in \mathcal{F}$ as follows: for the $k^{\text{th}}$ row of $f(C)$, we write $n$ ones in the columns $a_{n,k} - k + 1, a_{n-1,k} - k + 2, \dots, a_{1,k} - k + n$ (and we write zeros in the other cells in the row).
(a) Show that $f(C) \in \mathcal{F}$.
(b) Show that $f(f(f(f(f(f(C)))))) = C$ for any $C \in \mathcal{F}$.

ut.2013.2.8.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2013.2.8.reviewed_statement: Determine if there exists a (three-variable) polynomial $P(x, y, z)$ with integer coefficients satisfying the following property: a positive integer $n$ is not a perfect square if and only if there is a triple $(x, y, z)$ of positive integers such that $P(x, y, z) = n$.

ut.2014.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2014.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle, and let $X$ be a variable interior point on the minor arc $BC$ of its circumcircle. Let $P$ and $Q$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $X$ to lines $CA$ and $CB$, respectively. Let $R$ be the intersection of line $PQ$ and the perpendicular from $B$ to $AC$. Let $\ell$ be the line through $P$ parallel to $XR$. Prove that as $X$ varies along minor arc $BC$, the line $\ell$ always passes through a fixed point.

ut.2014.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2014.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots$ be a sequence of integers, with the property that every consecutive group of $a_i$'s averages to a perfect square. More precisely, for all positive integers $n$ and $k$, the quantity $$\frac{a_n + a_{n+1} + \cdots + a_{n+k-1}}{k}$$ is always the square of an integer. Prove that the sequence must be constant (all $a_i$ are equal to the same perfect square).

ut.2014.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2014.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be an even positive integer, and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex (simple) graph with exactly $\frac{n^2}{4}$ edges. An unordered pair of distinct vertices $\{x, y\}$ is said to be amicable if they have a common neighbor (there is a vertex $z$ such that $xz$ and $yz$ are both edges). Prove that $G$ has at least $2\binom{n/2}{2}$ pairs of vertices which are amicable.

ut.2014.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2014.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive even integer, and let $c_1, c_2, \dots, c_{n-1}$ be real numbers satisfying $$\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} |c_i - 1| < 1.$$ Prove that $$2x^n - c_{n-1}x^{n-1} + c_{n-2}x^{n-2} - \cdots - c_1x^1 + 2$$ has no real roots.

ut.2014.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2014.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral, and let $E$, $F$, $G$, and $H$ be the midpoints of $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, and $DA$ respectively. Let $W$, $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be the orthocenters of triangles $AHE$, $BEF$, $CFG$ and $DGH$, respectively. Prove that the quadrilaterals $ABCD$ and $WXYZ$ have the same area.

ut.2014.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2014.2.6.reviewed_statement:
For a prime $p$, a subset $S$ of residues modulo $p$ is called a sum-free multiplicative subgroup of $\mathbb{F}_p$ if
- there is a nonzero residue $\alpha$ modulo $p$ such that $S = \left\{1, \alpha^1, \alpha^2, \dots\right\}$ (all considered mod $p$), and
- there are no $a, b, c \in S$ (not necessarily distinct) such that $a + b \equiv c \pmod{p}$.
Prove that for every integer $N$, there is a prime $p$ and a sum-free multiplicative subgroup $S$ of $\mathbb{F}_p$ such that $|S| \ge N$.

ut.2015.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2015.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle with incenter $I$ whose incircle is tangent to $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$, respectively. Denote by $M$ the midpoint of $BC$ and let $P$ be a point in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ so that $MD = MP$ and $\angle PAB = \angle PAC$. Let $Q$ be a point on the incircle such that $\angle AQD = 90^\circ$. Prove that either $\angle PQE = 90^\circ$ or $\angle PQF = 90^\circ$.

ut.2015.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2015.1.2.reviewed_statement: Prove that for every positive integer $n$, there exists a set $S$ of $n$ positive integers such that for any two distinct $a, b \in S$, $a - b$ divides $a$ and $b$ but none of the other elements of $S$.

ut.2015.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2015.1.3.reviewed_statement: A physicist encounters $2015$ atoms called usamons. Each usamon either has one electron or zero electrons, and the physicist can't tell the difference. The physicist's only tool is a diode. The physicist may connect the diode from any usamon $A$ to any other usamon $B$. (This connection is directed.) When she does so, if usamon $A$ has an electron and usamon $B$ does not, then the electron jumps from $A$ to $B$. In any other case, nothing happens. In addition, the physicist cannot tell whether an electron jumps during any given step. The physicist's goal is to isolate two usamons that she is $100\%$ sure are currently in the same state. Is there any series of diode usage that makes this possible?

ut.2015.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2015.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $f : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}$ be a function such that for any $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}$, the number $f(x + y) - f(x) - f(y)$ is an integer. Decide whether there must exist a constant $c$ such that $f(x) - cx$ is an integer for every rational number $x$.

ut.2015.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2015.2.5.reviewed_statement: Fix a positive integer $n$. A tournament on $n$ vertices has all its edges colored by $\chi$ colors, so that any two directed edges $u \to v$ and $v \to w$ have different colors. Over all possible tournaments on $n$ vertices, determine the minimum possible value of $\chi$.

ut.2015.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2015.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a non-equilateral triangle and let $M_a$, $M_b$, $M_c$ be the midpoints of the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively. Let $S$ be a point lying on the Euler line. Denote by $X$, $Y$, $Z$ the second intersections of $M_aS$, $M_bS$, $M_cS$ with the nine-point circle. Prove that $AX$, $BY$, $CZ$ are concurrent.

ut.2016.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2016.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Let $S = \{1, \dots, n\}$. Given a bijection $f : S \to S$ an orbit of $f$ is a set of the form $\{x, f(x), f(f(x)), \dots\}$ for some $x \in S$. We denote by $c(f)$ the number of distinct orbits of $f$. For example, if $n = 3$ and $f(1) = 2$, $f(2) = 1$, $f(3) = 3$, the two orbits are $\{1, 2\}$ and $\{3\}$, hence $c(f) = 2$.
Given $k$ bijections $f_1, \dots, f_k$ from $S$ to itself, prove that $$c(f_1) + \cdots + c(f_k) \le n(k - 1) + c(f)$$ where $f : S \to S$ is the composed function $f_1 \circ \cdots \circ f_k$.

ut.2016.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2016.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a scalene triangle with circumcircle $\Omega$, and suppose the incircle of $ABC$ touches $BC$ at $D$. The angle bisector of $\angle A$ meets $BC$ and $\Omega$ at $K$ and $M$. The circumcircle of $\triangle DKM$ intersects the $A$-excircle at $S_1$, $S_2$, and $\Omega$ at $T \neq M$. Prove that line $AT$ passes through either $S_1$ or $S_2$.

ut.2016.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2016.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\mathbb{F}_p$ denote the integers modulo $p$, and let $\mathbb{F}_p[x]$ be the set of polynomials with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_p$. Define $\Psi : \mathbb{F}_p[x] \to \mathbb{F}_p[x]$ by $$\Psi\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n} a_i x^i\right) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} a_i x^{p^i}.$$ Prove that for nonzero polynomials $F, G \in \mathbb{F}_p[x]$, $$\Psi(\gcd(F, G)) = \gcd(\Psi(F), \Psi(G)).$$

ut.2016.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2016.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $\sqrt{3} = 1.b_1b_2b_3\dots_{(2)}$ be the binary representation of $\sqrt{3}$. Prove that for any positive integer $n$, at least one of the digits $b_n, b_{n+1}, \dots, b_{2n}$ equals $1$.

ut.2016.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2016.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $n \ge 4$ be an integer. Find all functions $W : \{1, \dots, n\}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for every partition $[n] = A \cup B \cup C$ into disjoint sets, $$\sum_{a \in A}\sum_{b \in B}\sum_{c \in C} W(a, b)W(b, c) = |A||B||C|.$$

ut.2016.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2016.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute scalene triangle and let $P$ be a point in its interior. Let $A_1$, $B_1$, $C_1$ be projections of $P$ onto triangle sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively. Find the locus of points $P$ such that $AA_1$, $BB_1$, $CC_1$ are concurrent and $\angle PAB + \angle PBC + \angle PCA = 90^\circ$.

ut.2017.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2017.1.1.reviewed_statement:
In a sports league, each team uses a set of at most $t$ signature colors. A set $S$ of teams is color-identifiable if one can assign each team in $S$ one of their signature colors, such that no team in $S$ is assigned any signature color of a different team in $S$.
For all positive integers $n$ and $t$, determine the maximum integer $g(n, t)$ such that: In any sports league with exactly $n$ distinct colors present over all teams, one can always find a color-identifiable set of size at least $g(n, t)$.

ut.2017.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2017.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABC$ be an acute scalene triangle with circumcenter $O$, and let $T$ be on line $BC$ such that $\angle TAO = 90^\circ$. The circle with diameter $AT$ intersects the circumcircle of $\triangle BOC$ at two points $A_1$ and $A_2$, where $OA_1 < OA_2$. Points $B_1$, $B_2$, $C_1$, $C_2$ are defined analogously.
(a) Prove that $AA_1$, $BB_1$, $CC_1$ are concurrent.
(b) Prove that $AA_2$, $BB_2$, $CC_2$ are concurrent on the Euler line of triangle $ABC$.

ut.2017.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2017.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $P, Q \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ be relatively prime nonconstant polynomials. Show that there can be at most three real numbers $\lambda$ such that $P + \lambda Q$ is the square of a polynomial.

ut.2017.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2017.2.4.reviewed_statement: You are cheating at a trivia contest. For each question, you can peek at each of the $n > 1$ other contestant's guesses before writing your own. For each question, after all guesses are submitted, the emcee announces the correct answer. A correct guess is worth $0$ points. An incorrect guess is worth $-2$ points for other contestants, but only $-1$ point for you, because you hacked the scoring system. After announcing the correct answer, the emcee proceeds to read out the next question. Show that if you are leading by $2^{n-1}$ points at any time, then you can surely win first place.

ut.2017.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2017.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with altitude $AE$. The $A$-excircle touches $BC$ at $D$, and intersects the circumcircle at two points $F$ and $G$. Prove that one can select points $V$ and $N$ on lines $DG$ and $DF$ such that quadrilateral $EVAN$ is a rhombus.

ut.2017.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2017.2.6.reviewed_statement: Prove that there are infinitely many triples $(a, b, p)$ of integers, with $p$ prime and $0 < a \le b < p$, for which $p^3$ divides $(a + b)^p - a^p - b^p$.

ut.2018.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2018.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n \ge 2$ be a positive integer, and let $\sigma(n)$ denote the sum of the positive divisors of $n$. Prove that the $n^{\text{th}}$ smallest positive integer relatively prime to $n$ is at least $\sigma(n)$, and determine for which $n$ equality holds.

ut.2018.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2018.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f : \mathbb{Z}^2 \to [0, 1]$ such that for any integers $x$ and $y$, $$f(x, y) = \frac{f(x - 1, y) + f(x, y - 1)}{2}.$$

ut.2018.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2018.1.3.reviewed_statement: At a university dinner, there are $2017$ mathematicians who each order two distinct entrées, with no two mathematicians ordering the same pair of entrées. The cost of each entrée is equal to the number of mathematicians who ordered it, and the university pays for each mathematician's less expensive entrée (ties broken arbitrarily). Over all possible sets of orders, what is the maximum total amount the university could have paid?

ut.2018.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2018.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $S \subseteq \{0, 1\}^n$ be a set of binary strings of length $n$. Given an odd number $x_1, \dots, x_{2k+1} \in S$ of binary strings (not necessarily distinct), their majority is defined as the binary string $y \in \{0, 1\}^n$ for which the $i^{\text{th}}$ bit of $y$ is the most common bit among the $i^{\text{th}}$ bits of $x_1, \dots, x_{2k+1}$. (For example, if $n = 4$ the majority of $0000$, $0000$, $1101$, $1100$, $0101$ is $0100$.)
Suppose that for some positive integer $k$, $S$ has the property $P_k$ that the majority of any $2k + 1$ binary strings in $S$ (possibly with repetition) is also in $S$. Prove that $S$ has the same property $P_k$ for all positive integers $k$.

ut.2018.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2018.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABCD$ be a convex cyclic quadrilateral which is not a kite, but whose diagonals are perpendicular and meet at $H$. Denote by $M$ and $N$ the midpoints of $\overline{BC}$ and $\overline{CD}$. Rays $MH$ and $NH$ meet $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{AB}$ at $S$ and $T$, respectively. Prove there exists a point $E$, lying outside quadrilateral $ABCD$, such that
- ray $EH$ bisects both angles $\angle BES$, $\angle TED$, and
- $\angle BEN = \angle MED$.

ut.2018.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2018.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Alice and Bob play a game. First, Alice secretly picks a finite set $S$ of lattice points in the Cartesian plane. Then, for every line $\ell$ in the plane which is horizontal, vertical, or has slope $+1$ or $-1$, she tells Bob the number of points of $S$ that lie on $\ell$. Bob wins if he can then determine the set $S$.
Prove that if Alice picks $S$ to be of the form $$S = \left\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \mid m \le x^2 + y^2 \le n\right\}$$ for some positive integers $m$ and $n$, then Bob can win. (Bob does not know in advance that $S$ is of this form.)

ut.2019.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2019.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle and let $M$ and $N$ denote the midpoints of $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Let $X$ be a point such that $AX$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Denote by $\omega_B$ the circle through $M$ and $B$ tangent to $MX$, and by $\omega_C$ the circle through $N$ and $C$ tangent to $NX$. Show that $\omega_B$ and $\omega_C$ intersect on line $BC$.

ut.2019.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2019.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ denote the set of integers considered modulo $n$ (hence $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ has $n$ elements). Find all positive integers $n$ for which there exists a bijective function $g : \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, such that the $101$ functions $$g(x), \quad g(x) + x, \quad g(x) + 2x, \quad \dots, \quad g(x) + 100x$$ are all bijections on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$.

ut.2019.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2019.1.3.reviewed_statement:
A snake of length $k$ is an animal which occupies an ordered $k$-tuple $(s_1, \dots, s_k)$ of cells in an $n \times n$ grid of square unit cells. These cells must be pairwise distinct, and $s_i$ and $s_{i+1}$ must share a side for $i = 1, \dots, k - 1$. If the snake is currently occupying $(s_1, \dots, s_k)$ and $s$ is an unoccupied cell sharing a side with $s_1$, the snake can move to occupy $(s, s_1, \dots, s_{k-1})$ instead. The snake has turned around if it occupied $(s_1, s_2, \dots, s_k)$ at the beginning, but after a finite number of moves occupies $(s_k, s_{k-1}, \dots, s_1)$ instead.
Determine whether there exists an integer $n > 1$ such that one can place some snake of length at least $0.9n^2$ in an $n \times n$ grid which can turn around.

ut.2019.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2019.2.4.reviewed_statement:
We say a function $f : \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \times \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{Z}$ is great if for any nonnegative integers $m$ and $n$, $$f(m + 1, n + 1)f(m, n) - f(m + 1, n)f(m, n + 1) = 1.$$ If $A = (a_0, a_1, \dots)$ and $B = (b_0, b_1, \dots)$ are two sequences of integers, we write $A \sim B$ if there exists a great function $f$ satisfying $f(n, 0) = a_n$ and $f(0, n) = b_n$ for every nonnegative integer $n$ (in particular, $a_0 = b_0$).
Prove that if $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are four sequences of integers satisfying $A \sim B$, $B \sim C$, and $C \sim D$, then $D \sim A$.

ut.2019.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2019.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Tasty and Stacy are given a circular necklace with $3n$ sapphire beads and $3n$ turquoise beads, such that no three consecutive beads have the same color. They play a cooperative game where they alternate turns removing three consecutive beads, subject to the following conditions:
- Tasty must remove three consecutive beads which are turquoise, sapphire, and turquoise, in that order, on each of his turns.
- Stacy must remove three consecutive beads which are sapphire, turquoise, and sapphire, in that order, on each of her turns.
They win if all the beads are removed in $2n$ turns. Prove that if they can win with Tasty going first, they can also win with Stacy going first.

ut.2019.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2019.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$, and let $D$ be a point on line $BC$ satisfying $\angle AID = 90^\circ$. Let the excircle of triangle $ABC$ opposite the vertex $A$ be tangent to $BC$ at point $A_1$. Define points $B_1$ on $CA$ and $C_1$ on $AB$ analogously, using the excircles opposite $B$ and $C$, respectively.
Prove that if quadrilateral $AB_1A_1C_1$ is cyclic, then $AD$ is tangent to the circumcircle of $\triangle DB_1C_1$.

ut.2020.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2020.1.1.reviewed_statement: Choose positive integers $b_1, b_2, \dots$ satisfying $$1 = \frac{b_1}{1^2} > \frac{b_2}{2^2} > \frac{b_3}{3^2} > \frac{b_4}{4^2} > \cdots$$ and let $r$ denote the largest real number satisfying $\frac{b_n}{n^2} \ge r$ for all positive integers $n$. What are the possible values of $r$ across all possible choices of the sequence $(b_n)$?

ut.2020.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2020.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Two circles $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ have common external tangents $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ meeting at $T$. Suppose $\ell_1$ touches $\Gamma_1$ at $A$ and $\ell_2$ touches $\Gamma_2$ at $B$. A circle $\Omega$ through $A$ and $B$ intersects $\Gamma_1$ again at $C$ and $\Gamma_2$ again at $D$, such that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is convex.
Suppose lines $AC$ and $BD$ meet at point $X$, while lines $AD$ and $BC$ meet at point $Y$. Show that $T$, $X$, $Y$ are collinear.

ut.2020.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2020.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Let $\alpha \ge 1$ be a real number. Hephaestus and Poseidon play a turn-based game on an infinite grid of unit squares. Before the game starts, Poseidon chooses a finite number of cells to be flooded. Hephaestus is building a levee, which is a subset of unit edges of the grid (called walls) forming a connected, non-self-intersecting path or loop.
The game then begins with Hephaestus moving first. On each of Hephaestus's turns, he adds one or more walls to the levee, as long as the total length of the levee is at most $\alpha n$ after his $n$th turn. On each of Poseidon's turns, every cell which is adjacent to an already flooded cell and with no wall between them becomes flooded as well.
Hephaestus wins if the levee forms a closed loop such that all flooded cells are contained in the interior of the loop — hence stopping the flood and saving the world. For which $\alpha$ can Hephaestus guarantee victory in a finite number of turns no matter how Poseidon chooses the initial cells to flood?

Note: More formally, there must exist lattice points $A_0, A_1, \dots, A_k$, pairwise distinct except possibly $A_0 = A_k$, such that the set of walls is exactly $\{A_0A_1, A_1A_2, \dots, A_{k-1}A_k\}$. Once a wall is built it cannot be destroyed; in particular, if the levee is a closed loop (i.e. $A_0 = A_k$) then Hephaestus cannot add more walls. Since each wall has length $1$, the length of the levee is $k$.

ut.2020.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2020.2.4.reviewed_statement:
For a finite simple graph $G$, we define $G'$ to be the graph on the same vertex set as $G$, where for any two vertices $u \neq v$, the pair $\{u, v\}$ is an edge of $G'$ if and only if $u$ and $v$ have a common neighbor in $G$.
Prove that if $G$ is a finite simple graph which is isomorphic to $(G')'$, then $G$ is also isomorphic to $G'$.

Note: A finite simple graph $G = (V, E)$ is a finite set $V$ of vertices, together with a set $E$ of edges, where each edge in $E$ is a set of two distinct vertices of $V$. If $v$ is a vertex of $G$, the neighbors of $v$ are the vertices $u$ for which $\{u, v\} \in E$. Two graphs $G_1 = (V_1, E_1)$ and $G_2 = (V_2, E_2)$ are isomorphic if there exists a bijection $f : V_1 \to V_2$ such that $\{u, v\} \in E_1$ if and only if $\{f(u), f(v)\} \in E_2$.

ut.2020.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2020.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Find all integers $n \ge 2$ for which there exists an integer $m$ and a polynomial $P(x)$ with integer coefficients satisfying the following three conditions:
- $m > 1$ and $\gcd(m, n) = 1$;
- the numbers $P(0), P^2(0), \dots, P^{m-1}(0)$ are not divisible by $n$; and
- $P^m(0)$ is divisible by $n$.
Here $P^k$ means $P$ applied $k$ times, so $P^1(0) = P(0)$, $P^2(0) = P(P(0))$, etc.

ut.2020.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2020.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Let $P_1P_2\cdots P_{100}$ be a cyclic $100$-gon, and let $P_i = P_{i+100}$ for all $i$. Define $Q_i$ as the intersection of diagonals $\overline{P_{i-2}P_{i+1}}$ and $\overline{P_{i-1}P_{i+2}}$ for all integers $i$.
Suppose there exists a point $P$ satisfying $\overline{PP_i} \perp \overline{P_{i-1}P_{i+1}}$ for all integers $i$. Prove that the points $Q_1, Q_2, \dots, Q_{100}$ are concyclic.

ut.2021.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2021.1.1.reviewed_statement: Determine all integers $s \ge 4$ for which there exist positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ such that $s = a + b + c + d$ and $s$ divides $abc + abd + acd + bcd$.

ut.2021.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2021.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Points $A$, $V_1$, $V_2$, $B$, $U_2$, $U_1$ lie fixed on a circle $\Gamma$, in that order, and such that $BU_2 > AU_1 > BV_2 > AV_1$.
Let $X$ be a variable point on the arc $V_1V_2$ of $\Gamma$ not containing $A$ or $B$. Line $XA$ meets line $U_1V_1$ at $C$, while line $XB$ meets line $U_2V_2$ at $D$. Let $O$ and $\rho$ denote the circumcenter and circumradius of $\triangle XCD$, respectively.
Prove there exists a fixed point $K$ and a real number $c$, independent of $X$, for which $OK^2 - \rho^2 = c$ always holds regardless of the choice of $X$.

ut.2021.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2021.1.3.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that satisfy the inequality $$f(y) - \left(\frac{z - y}{z - x}f(x) + \frac{y - x}{z - x}f(z)\right) \le f\left(\frac{x + z}{2}\right) - \frac{f(x) + f(z)}{2}$$ for all real numbers $x < y < z$.

ut.2023.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2023.1.1.reviewed_statement:
There are $2022$ equally spaced points on a circular track $\gamma$ of circumference $2022$. The points are labeled $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_{2022}$ in some order, each label used once. Initially, Bunbun the Bunny begins at $A_1$. She hops along $\gamma$ from $A_1$ to $A_2$, then from $A_2$ to $A_3$, until she reaches $A_{2022}$, after which she hops back to $A_1$. When hopping from $P$ to $Q$, she always hops along the shorter of the two arcs $\overset{\frown}{PQ}$ of $\gamma$; if $\overline{PQ}$ is a diameter of $\gamma$, she moves along either semicircle.
Determine the maximal possible sum of the lengths of the $2022$ arcs which Bunbun traveled, over all possible labellings of the $2022$ points.

ut.2023.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2023.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$, and let $E$ and $F$ be the feet of the altitudes from $B$ and $C$, respectively. Suppose that the common external tangents to the circumcircles of triangles $BME$ and $CMF$ intersect at a point $K$, and that $K$ lies on the circumcircle of $ABC$. ut.2023.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2023.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Let $\lfloor \bullet \rfloor$ denote the floor function. For nonnegative integers $a$ and $b$, their bitwise xor, denoted $a \oplus b$, is the unique nonnegative integer such that $$\left\lfloor \frac{a}{2^k} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{b}{2^k} \right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \frac{a \oplus b}{2^k} \right\rfloor$$ is even for every integer $k \ge 0$. (For example, $9 \oplus 10 = 1001_2 \oplus 1010_2 = 0011_2 = 3$.)
Find all positive integers $a$ such that for any integers $x > y \ge 0$, we have $$x \oplus ax \neq y \oplus ay.$$

ut.2023.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2023.2.5.reviewed_statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be fixed positive integers. Tsvety and Freyja play a game on an infinite grid of unit square cells. Tsvety has secretly written a real number inside of each cell so that the sum of the numbers within every rectangle of size either $m \times n$ or $n \times m$ is zero. Freyja wants to learn all of these numbers.
One by one, Freyja asks Tsvety about some cell in the grid, and Tsvety truthfully reveals what number is written in it. Freyja wins if, at any point, Freyja can simultaneously deduce the number written in every cell of the entire infinite grid. (If this never occurs, Freyja has lost the game and Tsvety wins.)
In terms of $m$ and $n$, find the smallest number of questions that Freyja must ask to win, or show that no finite number of questions can suffice.

ut.2023.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2023.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the set of positive integers. Fix a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and for any $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$ define $$\Delta(m, n) = \underbrace{f(f(\dots f}_{f(n)\text{ times}}(m)\dots)) - \underbrace{f(f(\dots f}_{f(m)\text{ times}}(n)\dots)).$$ Suppose $\Delta(m, n) \neq 0$ for any distinct $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$. Show that $\Delta$ is unbounded, meaning that for any constant $C$ there exist $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $|\Delta(m, n)| > C$.

ut.2024.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2024.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Find the smallest constant $C > 1$ such that the following statement holds: for every integer $n \ge 2$ and sequence of non-integer positive real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ satisfying $$\frac{1}{a_1} + \frac{1}{a_2} + \cdots + \frac{1}{a_n} = 1,$$ it's possible to choose positive integers $b_i$ such that
(i) for each $i = 1, 2, \dots, n$, either $b_i = \lfloor a_i \rfloor$ or $b_i = \lfloor a_i \rfloor + 1$; and
(ii) we have $$1 < \frac{1}{b_1} + \frac{1}{b_2} + \cdots + \frac{1}{b_n} \le C.$$
(Here $\lfloor \bullet \rfloor$ denotes the floor function, as usual.)

ut.2024.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2024.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$. Let segment $AI$ intersect the incircle of triangle $ABC$ at point $D$. Suppose that line $BD$ is perpendicular to line $AC$. Let $P$ be a point such that $\angle BPA = \angle PAI = 90^\circ$. Point $Q$ lies on segment $BD$ such that the circumcircle of triangle $ABQ$ is tangent to line $BI$. Point $X$ lies on line $PQ$ such that $\angle IAX = \angle XAC$. Prove that $\angle AXP = 45^\circ$.

ut.2024.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2024.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n > k \ge 1$ be integers and let $p$ be a prime dividing $\binom{n}{k}$. Prove that the $k$-element subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ can be split into $p$ classes of equal size, such that any two subsets with the same sum of elements belong to the same class.

ut.2025.1.1.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2025.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Ana and Banana play a game. Banana thinks of a function $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and a prime number $p$. He tells Ana that $f$ is nonconstant, $p < 100$, and $f(x + p) = f(x)$ for all integers $x$. Ana's goal is to determine the value of $p$. She writes down $n$ integers $x_1, \dots, x_n$. After seeing this list, Banana writes down $f(x_1), \dots, f(x_n)$ in order. Ana wins if she can determine the value of $p$ from this information. Find the smallest value of $n$ for which Ana has a winning strategy.

ut.2025.1.2.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2025.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1, a_2, \dots$ and $b_1, b_2, \dots$ be sequences of real numbers for which $a_1 > b_1$ and $$a_{n+1} = a_n^2 - 2b_n, \qquad b_{n+1} = b_n^2 - 2a_n$$ for all positive integers $n$. Prove that $a_1, a_2, \dots$ is eventually increasing (that is, there exists a positive integer $N$ for which $a_k < a_{k+1}$ for all $k > N$).

ut.2025.1.3.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2025.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Let $A_1A_2\cdots A_{2025}$ be a convex $2025$-gon, and let $A_i = A_{i+2025}$ for all integers $i$. Distinct points $P$ and $Q$ lie in its interior such that $\angle A_{i-1}A_iP = \angle QA_iA_{i+1}$ for all $i$. Define points $P_i^j$ and $Q_i^j$ for integers $i$ and positive integers $j$ as follows:
- For all $i$, $P_i^1 = Q_i^1 = A_i$.
- For all $i$ and $j$, $P_i^{j+1}$ and $Q_i^{j+1}$ are the circumcenters of $PP_i^jP_{i+1}^j$ and $QQ_i^jQ_{i+1}^j$, respectively.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ be the polygons $P_1^{2025}P_2^{2025}\cdots P_{2025}^{2025}$ and $Q_1^{2025}Q_2^{2025}\cdots Q_{2025}^{2025}$, respectively.
(a) Prove that $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ are cyclic.
(b) Let $O_P$ and $O_Q$ be the circumcenters of $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, respectively. Assuming that $O_P \neq O_Q$, show that $O_PO_Q$ is parallel to $PQ$.

ut.2025.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2025.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be collinear points such that $AY = AZ$, $BZ = BX$, and $CX = CY$. Points $X'$, $Y'$, and $Z'$ are the reflections of $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ over $BC$, $CA$, and $AB$, respectively. Prove that if $X'Y'Z'$ is a nondegenerate triangle, then its circumcenter lies on the circumcircle of $ABC$.

ut.2025.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2025.2.5.reviewed_statement: A pond has $2025$ lily pads arranged in a circle. Two frogs, Alice and Bob, begin on different lily pads. A frog jump is a jump which travels $2$, $3$, or $5$ positions clockwise. Alice and Bob each make a series of frog jumps, and each frog ends on the same lily pad that it started from. Given that each lily pad is the destination of exactly one jump, prove that each frog completes exactly two laps around the pond (i.e. travels $4050$ positions in total).

ut.2026.2.4.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2026.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. In the infinite lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$, $n$ points are colored red while the rest are colored blue. Each red point is labeled with the distance to the nearest blue point in the same row or column. Find the smallest real number $\alpha$ for which the sum of all labels does not exceed $100n^{\alpha}$, independent of $n$ and the placement of the red points.
(Note: A row is the set of points with a given $y$-coordinate, and a column is the set of points with a given $x$-coordinate.)

ut.2026.2.5.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review

Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of triangle formed by $BC$ and the two common external tangents of the circumcircles $ABM$ and $ACM$. Prove that the internal bisector of $\angle BAC$ and the perpendicular bisector of $AM$ intersect on the radical axis of $\omega$ and $\Gamma$.

ut.2026.2.6.scope: Statement fidelity only; no solution or independent mathematical correctness review
ut.2026.2.6.reviewed_statement: A positive integer is called chaotic if it can be expressed as $a^3 + b^3 + abc$ for positive integers $a \ge b \ge c$. Show that there is no infinite increasing arithmetic progression consisting of only chaotic positive integers.

Year labels denote selection cycles; exams may start in December of the preceding calendar year. The 2012 PDF has an inconsistent 54th IMO header; its printed exam dates are December 15, 2011 and February 1, 2012. be.2022.0.4.reviewed_statement:
A school has $590$ pupils, to be divided into $25$ classes, each containing between $18$ and $28$ pupils.

(a) Can the pupils be divided so that $22$ classes have the same size?

(b) Find the largest integer $n$ for which some division has $n$ classes of the same size.

(c) Can the pupils be divided so that no three classes have the same size?

(d) Find the largest integer $n$ such that every division has at least $n$ classes of the same size.

itt.2010.1.1.reviewed_statement:
There are $n$ cards, where $n\ge50$ is an integer. Each card has one black side and one blue side. Initially the cards lie in a row on a table, all showing their blue sides. Alberto and Barbara, standing on the same side of the table, take turns choosing a block of $50$ consecutive cards whose leftmost card is blue, and turning over all the cards in that block. Alberto starts. The game ends when no legal move is possible; the player making the last legal move wins.

(a) Prove that the game terminates for every $n$.

(b) Determine, in terms of $n$, which player has a winning strategy.

itt.2010.1.2.reviewed_statement: A cyclic quadrilateral has the property that the midpoints of its sides also form a cyclic quadrilateral. Prove that the area of the disk bounded by the circumcircle of the smaller quadrilateral is at most half the area of the disk bounded by the circumcircle of the larger quadrilateral.

itt.2010.2.5.reviewed_statement: A football tournament has $n\ge3$ teams. Each team plays each other team exactly once. A win earns $3$ points, a loss $0$ points, and a draw $1$ point for each team. At the end, all teams have distinct point totals forming an arithmetic progression, and the last-place team has exactly one point. Determine all possible configurations: the value of $n$, the final standings, and the results of every match.

itt.2011.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $n>1$ be odd. Let $S$ be the set of integers $k$ with $1\le k\le n$ that are relatively prime to $n$, and let $T$ be the set of $k\in S$ for which $k+1$ is relatively prime to $n$. For each $k\in S$, let $r_k$ be the remainder on division by $n$ of $$\frac{k^{|S|}-1}{n}.$$ Prove that $$\prod_{k\in T}(r_k-r_{n-k})\equiv |S|^{|T|}\pmod n.$$

itt.2012.2.6.reviewed_statement:

(a) Find all functions $f$ from the positive integers to the positive integers such that $$f^{(n+1)}(n)<f(n+1)$$ for every positive integer $n$.

(b) Find all pairs $(f,g)$ of functions from the positive integers to the positive integers such that $$f^{(g(n)+1)}(n)+g^{(f(n))}(n)=f(n+1)-g(n+1)+1$$ for every positive integer $n$.

cl.2013.0.1.reviewed_statement: Prove that the equation $$x^x+y^y=z^z$$ has no solutions in integers.
cl.2013.0.1.text: Source domain note: the official paper asks for integer solutions but does not specify a convention for 0^0. The printed domain is preserved; no additional convention is assumed.

cl.2023.2.6.reviewed_statement: For $n=0,1,2,\ldots$, consider the sequence $$a_n=4^n c+\frac{4^n-(-1)^n}{5}.$$ Determine the values of $c$ for which the sequence contains a perfect square.
cl.2023.2.6.text: Source domain note: the official paper does not specify the domain of the parameter c. This omission is preserved rather than silently imposing an integer or real domain.

cl.2024.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $m\ge2$ and $k\ge1$ be integers. Prove that $$(m-1)^2\mid m^k-1\quad\text{if and only if}\quad m-1\mid k.$$
cl.2024.1.2.text: Editorial domain clarification: m ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1. The handwritten original gives m, k as natural numbers without excluding m = 1, which would make the divisibility assertion involve a zero divisor.

cl.2025.2.7.reviewed_statement: Determine all functions $f:\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\}\to\mathbb R$ such that $$f(x)+f\left(\frac1{1-x}\right)=x$$ for every $x\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\}$.
cl.2025.2.7.text: Editorial domain clarification: the equation is required for x in R excluding 0 and 1, matching the declared domain of f. The official paper instead prints “for every x in R”, where the expressions are undefined at those two points.

tht.2015.10.33.reviewed_statement: The price of a real sequence $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ is $\max_{1\le i\le n}|x_1+\cdots+x_i|$. Given $n$ real numbers, Dave checks every ordering and obtains the minimum price $D$. George chooses $x_1$ with minimum $|x_1|$, then at step $i$ chooses a remaining number $x_i$ minimizing $|x_1+\cdots+x_i|$, breaking ties randomly. His resulting price is $G$. Find the least constant $c$ such that $G\le cD$ for every positive integer $n$, every collection of $n$ real numbers, and every possible ordering produced by George.

tht.2015.11.37.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a fixed acute triangle. For points $E\in AC,F\in AB$, let $M$ be the midpoint of $EF$, and let its perpendicular bisector meet $BC$ at $K$. The perpendicular bisector of $MK$ meets $AC,AB$ at $S,T$. Call $(E,F)$ interesting if $KSAT$ is cyclic. tht.2011.10.28.reviewed_statement: Define $K_0=1$ and $K_n=1+\min\{2K_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor},3K_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}\}$ for integers $n\ge1$. Prove or disprove that $K_n\ge n$ for every integer $n\ge0$.
tht.2011.10.28.text: Editorial clarification: the source gives K_0 = 1 but prints the recurrence for n ≥ 0, which conflicts at zero. The recurrence is stated here for n ≥ 1; its conclusion still includes n = 0.

tht.2011.14.42.reviewed_statement: Let $A_1,A_2,A_3,A_4$ be points in the plane with $A_4$ the centroid of triangle $A_1A_2A_3$. Find a point $A_5$ maximising $$\frac{\min_{1\le i<j<k\le5}A_iA_jA_k}{\max_{1\le i<j<k\le5}A_iA_jA_k}.$$
tht.2011.14.42.text: Source ambiguity: A_iA_jA_k is not defined. The source itself asks whether this denotes triangle area. The ratio is retained without inventing that convention.

tht.2012.9.25.reviewed_statement: Given a positive integer $n$, prove that there are only finitely many monic polynomials of degree $n$ with integer coefficients whose zeros all lie in $\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|\le1\}$. Also prove that every zero of each such polynomial has modulus $0$ or $1$.
tht.2012.9.25.text: Editorial correction, awaiting an independent source: the source prints “infinitely many” fixed-degree monic integer polynomials. The record states “only finitely many”; this correction is explicit and is not certified as original contest wording.

tht.2012.9.26.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b$ be positive integers. Suppose $\gcd(\Phi_a(t),\Phi_b(t))>1$ for some positive integer $t$, where $\Phi_j$ is the $j$th cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that $a/b=p^k$ for a prime $p$ and an integer $k$.
tht.2012.9.26.text: Notation correction: the source switches its evaluation variable from t to k within the question. A single positive integer t is used consistently here.

tht.2013.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and $G=\{z\in\mathbb C:z^n=1\}$. Find all functions $f:G\to\mathbb Z$ satisfying (i) $f(z)=1$ if and only if $z=1$; and (ii) $f(z^k)=\frac{f(z)}{\gcd(f(z),k)}$ for all $z\in G$ and all positive integers $k$.
tht.2013.1.2.text: Notation correction: condition (ii) quantifies n in the source, although its displayed variable is k. The quantifier here uses k.

tht.2013.3.7.reviewed_statement: Let $S$ be a set of students with $|S|\ge4$. There is a positive integer $m$ with $3\le m\le|S|-1$ such that, for every $A\subseteq S$ with $|A|=m$, exactly one student is friends with every student in $A$. No student is friends with themself. Prove that either (i) a subset $B\subseteq S$ with $|B|=m+1$ consists of pairwise friends; or (ii) $|S|=m+1$.
tht.2013.3.7.text: Source ambiguity: the source footnote explicitly questions whether the conclusion is (i) or (ii), or both. The printed “either … or” is retained.

tht.2013.4.10.text: Potential source typo: the middle denominator is printed z(y+z)+x(y+z). This is retained literally without replacing it by a cyclic expression.

tht.2013.10.29.reviewed_statement: Let $(a_1,\ldots,a_{2n})$ be a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,2n\}$ such that the values $|a_{i+1}-a_1|$, for $1\le i\le2n-1$, are distinct. Prove that $a_1-a_{2n}=n$ if and only if $1\le a_{2k}\le n$ for each $1\le k\le n$.
tht.2013.10.29.text: Potential source typo: the source prints |a_{i+1}−a_1|, not consecutive differences. Its condition is retained literally and has not been mathematically certified.

tht.2013.10.30.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{>0}$, and write $f^m$ for its $m$-fold iterate. For every positive integer $n$, suppose there is a positive integer $k$ with $f^{2k}(n)=n+k$. Let $k_n$ be the least such positive integer. Prove that $k_1,k_2,\ldots$ is unbounded.
tht.2013.10.30.text: Convention clarification: the source uses N for the iteration parameter. Positive k is used here, since allowing k = 0 would trivialize the stated minimum.

tht.2014.4.13.reviewed_statement: Every pair among $n$ towns is connected by a one-way or two-way road. For every $k$ towns, there is a round trip through each of those $k$ towns exactly once. Find the largest possible number of one-way roads.
tht.2014.4.13.text: Source omission: the source does not specify or quantify the parameter k. This omission remains unresolved; no range or fixed value is inferred.

tht.2014.7.24.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be scalene, with incircle centred at $I$ of radius $r$, touching $BC,CA,AB$ at $X,Y,Z$. Choose $X_1,Y_1,Z_1$ on rays $IX,IY,IZ$ with $IX_1=IY_1=IZ_1=2r$. Prove that (a) $AX_1,BY_1,CZ_1$ concur at a point $Q$; and (b) if $O$ is the circumcentre of $ABC$ and $P$ is the intersection of $OI$ with the reflection of $AQ$ across $AI$, then $\angle PCI=\angle ICQ$.
tht.2014.7.24.text: Notation correction: the source calls O the circumcircle while using line OI. O is rendered as the circumcentre here, consistently with the construction.
